name: ALS SubZero
description: Dynamic delay-line network memory filesystem that stores data in flight across IP network paths with zero local disk writes and Cauchy Reed-Solomon erasure coding.
abstract: ALS SubZero turns network packet propagation delay into volatile, self-healing memory. Data is chunked into 4096-byte blocks, encoded with Cauchy Reed-Solomon parity over GF(2^8), framed with 24-byte binary headers (magic ALS1) and Castagnoli CRC32C checksums, and continuously circulated across remote IP echo reflectors. A microsecond-precision departure pacer prevents socket saturation, and an autonomous parity scrubber reconstructs missing chunks in flight under packet loss rates up to 10.0%.
softwareRequirements: GCC or Clang (optional, for C native build)
